neighbours.label: technical vocabulary of statistical estimation and machine learning (unbiased estimator, leaf nodes, shrinking variance), as against the same words used in everyday senses
fire: Under the Gauss-Markov conditions, least squares gives the best linear unbiased estimates.
Each leaf node of the regression tree stores the mean of its training points.
As the number of samples grows, the variance of the estimate shrinks toward zero.
The ridge estimator is biased, but its variance shrinks as the penalty grows.
Pruning removes leaf nodes that do not reduce the validation error.
The weighted estimator remains unbiased when the weights sum to one.
Bootstrap resampling gives an estimate of the standard error of the median.
A random forest averages the predictions stored at the leaves of many trees.
quiet: The newspaper promised readers fair and unbiased reporting of the election.
Each leaf of the old oak tree turned yellow by early October.
As the days get colder, the wool sweater shrinks in the hot wash.
The shop owner was biased toward regular customers, but his prices were fair.
The gardener removes dead leaves that fall onto the lawn.
The referee remained unbiased even when the crowd booed loudly.
The builder gave an estimate of the cost of the new kitchen.
A big forest grows slowly from the seeds dropped by many trees.
